sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This guide contains information on how to create mods for Conquest of Elysium 5, to change aspects of the game or to add new content.

sections.title: General Information
paragraphs: With the help of a simple text editor it is possible to create new weapons, units and entire classes. It is also possible to modify existing weapons, units, classes, spells and magic items.

Conquest of Elysium 5 mods are text files with a series of commands that the game interprets and uses to alter the desired objects.  The file extension for CoE5 mods is .c5m. The mod files must be located within a subdirectory of the mods directory of CoE5, which you may open from the main menu.  Everything in a mod (including the .c5m file) must be placed in a subdirectory with the same name as your mod. The .c5m file must also have the name of your mod plus '.c5m' at the end. The mod name must not include any spaces or special characters.

With the help of a paint program you will also be able to add new graphics to units or terrain.  All images must be saved as Targa (.tga) or PNG (.png) images.  TGA image files must have 24- or 32-bit color and be uncompressed or RLE.  If the image is saved as a TGA file that doesn’t have any transparent pixels, black (0,0,0) will be replaced with a fully transparent color and magenta (255,0,255) will be replaced by a shadow color. In this manual image files are often written as "image.tga", but a PNG file can be used intead.

sections.title: Mod Mechanics
paragraphs: Regardless of content, all CoE5 mods have a similar structure.  All modding commands must be saved in a text file with the .c5m (Conquest of Elysium 5 mod) extension.  The c5m file must be located within a subdirectory of the CoE5 mod directory.

It is possible to have many mods enabled at once.  For instance you can enable a mod that turns Dwarves into giants at the same time as a mod that adds a new Elf nation.  A game created when a mod is active will automatically activate this mod for all players participating in that game.  There will be an error message for any player who hasn’t downloaded the mod.  Two mods should never try to modify the same thing.  This can result in different behavior on different computers.

Mod commands are executed from the beginning of the file to the end of the file.  Make sure that commands that are prerequisites for others appear before the commands that require them.  For example, modding a new weapon must be done before assigning it to a new monster (or an existing monster) or the mod will crash.

sections.title: Mod Syntax
paragraphs: Mods commands are mainly a text command followed by numbers and perhaps some text (e.g. naming something).
A hash-sign (#) indicates a comment and anything after it will be ignored.
The mod commands sometimes have a vertical line (|) among their arguments.  This line means OR. So use either the argument on the left side of the line or the one on the other side, not both.
When a mod command has an argument inside brackets like [<value>], it means that it is an optional argument that can be omitted (also, never write the brackets [] when using the command).
An argument of <0-1> means 0=disabled, 1=enabled. Usually you always want to use a 1 here, unless you want to disable an already existing ability.
Make sure to have correct UPPER/lower-case letters for filenames.  The Linux filesystem is case sensitive and mods won’t work if they are mixed up.

Many commands take a monster name as an argument. This name can also have an offset before the monster name if you don’t want to select the first or sometimes a random one. paragraphs: Mods can be uploaded to the Steam Workshop which will allow other users to download and enjoy them.  This example creates a minimal mod called "orcking" that is ready to be published on the Steam Workshop.  Once the mod is ready it can be uploaded by selecting mods from the main menu and right clicking on the mod, there will be an "Upload mod to Steam Workshop" button there.

paragraphs: This file determines who can see the mod on steam. The value of Visibility can be one of these three: private/friends/public.

sections.title: Mod Info
paragraphs: This gives some basic information about the mod that can be shown to the user when choosing what mods to enable. The first two Mod Info commands are required for all mods.

sections.title: Maps
paragraphs: Mods can also include premade maps, enabling modders to create map packs that can be uploaded to the workshop. The map file must be placed in the same folder as everything else in the mod.

sections.title: Fonts & Translation
paragraphs: Fonts can also include ttf fonts, enabling modders to use special fonts for translation mods. The font file must be placed in the same folder as everything else in the mod. To get hold of all translatable strings you should play the game with the "--dumpstrings" start option. That will create a file called "transtrings.txt" that contains all strings (text snippets) encountered while playing that hasn’t been translated by any currently enabled mod. Sometimes the strings will contain something like "%s" or "%d". This will be replaced by another string or number later, these special characters must be present in the translated version as well.

sections.title: Weapon Modding
paragraphs: These commands can be used to modify or create new weapons.

sections.title: Magic Item Modding
paragraphs: These commands can be used to modify or create new magic items.

sections.title: Monster Commands for Magic Items
paragraphs: These commands are exactly the same as the monster command with the same name, look at monster modding for information on how to use them. They can be used for magic items too.

sections.title: Monster Modding
paragraphs: These commands allow the modifying of existing monsters and creating new monsters. At most about 3000 new monsters can be created by mods.

sections.title: Attacks
paragraphs: Weapon number can be used to select the weapon instead of name if needed. Weapons that can be replaced by items (e.g. Broadsword or Spear) have fixed damage values and the damage value set by mod command becomes a damage bonus for the monster.

Note that for weapons that do special effect damage (damage type 12) or special benefit damage (damage type 13), the damage value in the weapon commands is a bitmask value that specifies what effect or effects take place.
The asterisk damage notation of means variable damage and the # means the weapon uses a bitmask to create a special effect.

Special weapon properties such as Drain, Strikes Rear, Strikes Anywhere, Negates Shields etc are intrinsic properties of the weapon and must be assigned by weapon modding before the weapons are given to a monster.

sections.title: Combat Spells
paragraphs: These commands set the spell casting abilities of the monster. Spell casting abilities work exactly like weapons, with the difference that the spell to be cast is selected randomly from the spells the monster has memorized. Each spell has the role of a weapon when cast.
Magic paths are listed in the Table Magic Paths (path) . Spell casting level is a value from 1 to 3. There are no higher spell casting levels.

sections.title: Movement
paragraphs: These commands determines how fast the monster can move over different map terrains as well as how it will move in combat.

sections.title: Behavior
paragraphs: Most of these commands determine how a monster will try to act when it is independent owned. But it will also determine how player owned creates with the Stupid tag acts. Terrains ending in 1 (e.g. swamp1) means the monster loves this terrain type and will never leave it for a non-loved terrain. If it ends in 2 (e.g. swamp2) the monster likes the terrain type and may leave it, but not go more than 1 square away from it.

sections.title: Class Modding
paragraphs: These commands are used to modify and create new playable classes. A maximum of about 150 new classes can be added by mods.

sections.title: Recruitment List
paragraphs: These commands govern the recruitment list of a class. A recruitment list can have a maximum of 128 units on it.

sections.title: Terrain Modding
paragraphs: These commands allow the modding of world map terrain types. To find out what number a certain type of terrain has, press ctrl+i in the game and it will show the number of the terrain in that square.

sections.title: Terrain Group Modding
paragraphs: These commands can be used to create new terrain groups, i.e. negative terrain numbers that corresponds to a bunch of terrains. They have a negative number from -1000 to -1199, a name e.g. "castles and temples" and finally a number of terrains that fulfills the requirement for this terrain group.

sections.title: Ritual Modding
paragraphs: These commands are used to modify existing rituals or construct new schools of rituals and the individual rituals within that school.

sections.title: Mastery Commands
paragraphs: These commands are usually used for different mastery rituals. They will grant new spells and upgrade the caster to a new monster type.

sections.title: Targeting Commands
paragraphs: These commands sets the Target Location or Target Unit for the ritual. By default these targets are the caster and his square. This is fine for normal summoning and mastery rituals and usually only more exotic rituals that targets squares or units far away have any need to change this.

sections.title: Sound Sample Modding
paragraphs: This command can be used to modify or create new sound samples. These can then be used as sound effects for weapons and rituals in the mod.

sections.title: Misc Modding
paragraphs: For those commands that do not fit into one of the usual categories.

sections.title: Events
paragraphs: Events are composed of one start command, usually one or more triggers, one or more actions and finally the end command.
The trigger determines when the event will happen and the action determines what will happen as the result.
Events can be added both to mods and to custom map files.

sections.title: Event Triggers
paragraphs: Restricts when the event can occur. Note that all triggers can be inverted by writing - instead of +.

sections.title: Set variables
paragraphs: All variables are set to zero when the game begins.

sections.title: Special Values
paragraphs: Where a "player" number is required one of these numbers can be used.

sections.title: Updating a Mod
paragraphs: Updating a mod might break old saved games using that mod unless you take some special care.

Any new units have to added after all previous units and any new classes after all other classes and so on. If updates are done in this way, saves should remain compatible. Adding a new unit in the middle of a mod will shuffle around all the ones behind it and break any saved games.

commands.name: icon
commands.description: Icon shown when selecting the mod in CoE5. It should be a 256*64 large TGA or PNG image.

commands.name: description
commands.description: A text description of the mod.

commands.name: modprio
commands.description: Sets when this mod should be loaded in relation to other mods. Default is 5 and lower numbers are loaded first. Usually you don’t need to use this command.

commands.name: mapfile
commands.description: The filename of the map. A single mod can contain many maps.

commands.name: fontfile
commands.description: The filename of the font. Font nbr 0 = standard, 1 = fancy (used for headers), 2 = long texts (for descriptions).

commands.name: translation
commands.description: Translates all occurances of the "from" text to the "to" text.

commands.name: newweapon
commands.description: This command creates a new weapon.

commands.name: selectweapon
commands.description: Selects an existing weapon for modification. There may be several different weapons with the same name, in which case you should use the weapon number for selecting the desired weapon. You can see existing weapon numbers in game by pressing ctrl-i when inspecting a unit.

commands.name: trgrank
commands.description: Sets the battlefield row where the weapon hits. See the Target Ranks (trgrank) table for the possible values. The default value is 1.

commands.name: range
commands.description: The maximum range of the weapon. This should be 1 for melee weapons. A normal bow has range 5.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Initiative value for the weapon, default is 2. Some common initiative values are these 1=spell, 2=fist/dagger/bow, 3=club/axe, 4=sword, 6=spear.

commands.name: dmgtype
commands.description: Sets the damage type for the weapon. Table Damage Types (dmgtype) contains the list of possible damage types. The default value is 3 (piercing damage).

commands.name: dmg
commands.description: Sets the damage for the weapon. The default value is 0, which makes the weapon a natural weapon whose base damage is determined during monster modding. Note that damage types 12 and 13 require a bitmask value for their special effects. The special afflictions and benefit effects are listed in table Special Afflictions and table Special Benefits .

commands.name: aoe
commands.description: Sets the area of effect for the weapon in squares. The default value is 0 (a single monster). A value of x will hit up to x monsters near the target. There are also many special values that can be used for other kind of areas. See Table Area of Effects (aoe) . Those that are written as e.g. 30xx must be written as a 4 digit number e.g. “aoe 3005” for a cone of 5 squares.

commands.name: look
commands.description: Sets the visual effect that occurs where the weapon strikes down, e.g. a fiery explosion for a fireball. See the Visual Effects (look) table. The default is no visual effect.

commands.name: sound
commands.description: The sound effect when the weapon strikes down. See table Sound Effects (sound) .

commands.name: flymode
commands.description: Set this if a projectile should be visible for a ranged attack. See Fly modes (flymode) table. Those marked with an asterisk (*) behave like normal for aoe 1 effects, but with larger aoe they still only create one flying graphical effect. Fireball uses this effect to create a single flying fireball, but with a larger aoe explosion. If using a sprite (flymode 1) then the look value will be used to set the sprite used. See the table Fly Sprites (flyspr) for possible sprites to use.

commands.name: flylook
commands.description: The visual effect (see table Visual Effects (look) ) of the flying projectile, ranged weapons only. If flymode is 1 a fly sprite (see table Fly Sprites (flyspr) ) should be used instead of a look number.

commands.name: flysound
commands.description: The sound effect when the projectile starts flying, ranged weapons only. -1 = none.

commands.name: sndvol
commands.description: dvol -50 = half volume, 100 = double volume.

commands.name: reloadsnd
commands.description: Sound when reloading, -1 = none.

commands.name: yellow
commands.description: set color of damage numbers

commands.name: blue
commands.description: set color of damage numbers

commands.name: purple
commands.description: set color of damage numbers

commands.description: If the target is wounded by the weapon, it will also be hit by the next weapon, i.e. the weapon defined next in the mod after this weapon. This command can only be used for new weapons, so you must have created one with the newweapon command.

commands.name: nextwep
commands.description: Like 'next' but the additional strike will come from a named weapon that has already been created.

commands.name: nextalways
commands.description: Like next, but will take effect even if no damage was inflicted on the target.

commands.name: nextalwayswep
commands.description: Like 'nextalways' but the additional strike will come from a named weapon that has already been created.

commands.name: nextdmg

commands.name: reload2

commands.name: reload3

commands.description: A victim killed by this weapon becomes a monster of the type that immediately follows the killer in the monster list. For example, units killed by a Doppelganger become Doppelspawn, which is the next unit in order from Doppelganger.

commands.name: replicate

commands.name: ethereal

commands.name: mind

commands.name: sweep

commands.name: affectmale

commands.name: stone

commands.name: wallkill
commands.description: x5 dmg vs walls and boats

commands.name: flying2

commands.name: targterr

commands.name: soft

commands.name: tree

commands.name: newitem
commands.description: This command creates a new magic item.

commands.name: selectitem
commands.description: Selects an existing magic item for modification.

commands.name: name
commands.description: Set the name of the magic item. Not necessary if you created a new one with newitem.

commands.name: descr
commands.description: Not necessary, as most magic items don’t have descriptions.

commands.name: spr
commands.description: Sets the sprite for the magic item. It should be centered in a 32x32 or 64x64 pixel large image. The drawn item should not be larger than 40x40 pixels however, so if put in a 64x64 image it should be surrounded by black.

commands.name: rarity
commands.description: Sets how easy it should be to find this item. 0=common, 1=rare, 2=rare & unique, 3=impossible to find as a random item. Default is 0.

commands.name: type
commands.description: Sets the magic item type. Default is 7 = misc item. See table Magic Item Types

commands.name: itemwep
commands.description: Sets the weapon stats of the magic item to those of the weapon with this name. Only use this together with type 1 magic items.

commands.name: armor
commands.description: Armor value, default 0.

commands.name: protection
commands.description: Protection bonus, default 0.

commands.name: hp
commands.description: Hit Point bonus, default 0.

commands.name: combatsum
commands.description: Mode -1 = will summon on the first round of combat, 1 = will summon on all rounds of combat. Summoning string is very similar to the summoning strings used for ritual summoning. E.g. "2d4*Deer & 2*wolf" would summon 2-8 deer and 2 wolves. Commanders cannot be summoned in battle.

commands.name: combatspell
commands.description: Mode -1 = spell will be auto cast on the first round, 1 = unit can cast this spell (like a wand), 2 = spell will be auto cast each round. The spell name is simply the name of the combat spell to be cast, e.g. "Fireball".

commands.name: copyspr
commands.description: Uses the sprite from this magic item.

commands.name: copystats
commands.description: Copies all stats except the name from this magic item.

commands.name: selectmonster
commands.description: Selects the monster that will be affected by the following modding commands. The selected monster is referred to as the active monster. The selectmonster command always selects the first monster of that name in the monster list. If there is more than one monster with the same name (e.g. longdead) the offset value can be used to select them. Leave the offset out if you only want to select the first monster. The default value of the offset is 0. The offset used by this command cannot be set to a negative value, unlike the offset for the lookslike command. Offset value 1 means the command selects the (first + 1) monster of that name, i.e. the second monster. Offset 2 selects the third monster of the same name etc. Note that this command cannot use the "1:spearman" syntax.

commands.name: newmonster
commands.description: Creates a new monster. This new monster will be affected by the following modding commands until the next active monster is set. The monster can have the same name as another monster.

commands.name: name
commands.description: This command renames an existing monster. It is not needed when creating a new monster.

commands.name: spr1
commands.description: The file name of the normal image for the monster. This command sets the attack sprite to this image as well.The image should be 32x32 or 64x64 for normal sized monsters and 128x128 for huge monsters. A human being should be about 34 pixels tall and there should be 2 pixels of free space between his feet and the bottom of the image.

commands.name: spr2
commands.description: The file name of the attack image for the monster. If this is not set, then spr1 will be used for this image too. This command must come after the spr1 command.

commands.name: descr
commands.description: Description of the monster. The ^ character will be replaced with a newline.

commands.name: hp
commands.description: The maximum number of hit points for the monster. A normal human soldier has 6 hit points and an elite heavily armored soldier has 10 hit points. An ogre has 25 hit points, a troll has 56 hit points and giants, dragons and other huge monsters can have well over a 100 hit points.

commands.name: mr
commands.description: The magic resistance of the monster. Animals have a magic resistance of 2, a normal human has 4 and a more susceptible human has 3. Apprentice mages have a magic resistance of 6, full mages have 8 and master mages have 9. Some highly magical beings may have even higher magic resistance and they can almost never be affected by magic that is resistible.

commands.name: str
commands.description: The strength of the monster. A normal human soldier has a strength of 4, an elite human soldier has 5, a troll has 8 or 9 and giants and dragons have 10 to 12.

commands.name: armor
commands.description: This command sets the monster’s armor value, which represents its natural protection or the armor it is wearing. Normal human troops have an armor value of 0. Medium armored human troops have an armor value of 1. Heavily armored human troops like Heavy Infantry have an armor value of 2 and very heavily armored troops like Knights and High Lords have an armor value of 3. Extremely tough monsters like dragons may have an armor value of 4 or more.

commands.name: mor
commands.description: The morale of the monster. A normal human soldier has a morale of 4, an elite human soldier has 5 or 6 and powerful monsters can have a morale of 8 or more. Very fearless monsters may have a morale of 15. Setting the morale to 99 makes the monster Mindless and it will be completely unaffected by fear or any other effects that influence morale.

commands.name: rank
commands.description: Sets the default deployment rank for the monster. -1 = back, 0 = mid, 1 = front

commands.name: copystats
commands.description: Copies the attributes, weapons, graphics and other properties of the specified monster. The command does not copy the name of the monster, however.

commands.name: copyspr
commands.description: Copy the sprite of another monster.

commands.name: clearspec
commands.description: Removes all special abilities from the active monster. The special abilities are things like Fire Immunity, Regeneration, etc. This command does not clear movement abilities. Use the clearmove command for that.

commands.name: clearmove
commands.description: Removes all movement attributes from the active monster.

commands.name: clearweapons
commands.description: Removes all weapons from the active monster.

commands.name: meleeweapon
commands.description: Equips the monster with a melee weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>.

commands.name: meleeweaponbonus
commands.description: Equips the monster with a melee weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon will be used in addition to any other attacks the monster has.

commands.name: meleeweaponspec
commands.description: Equips the monsters with a special melee weapon. Any normal melee attacks after this one will not be used if this attack was used. Normally used for lances.

commands.name: meleeweaponlong
commands.description: This command is deprecated and should no longer be used.

commands.name: meleeweapon50s
commands.description: Equips the monster with a melee+skip attack that has 50% chance of being used. If it is used the next attack will  be skipped.

commands.name: rangedweapon
commands.description: Equips the monster with a ranged weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>.

commands.name: rangedweaponbonus
commands.description: Equips the monster with a ranged weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon will be used in addition to any other attacks the monster has.

commands.name: rangedweapon25
commands.description: Equips the monster with a ranged weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon has a 25% chance of being used in melee combat.

commands.name: rangedweapon50
commands.description: Equips the monster with a ranged weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon has a 50% chance of being used in melee combat.

commands.name: rangedweapon50s
commands.description: Equips the monster with a range+skip weapon that has 50% chance of being used in melee (100% at range). When used the next weapon will be skipped.

commands.name: rangedweapon50x
commands.description: Equips the monster with a range+skip weapon that has 50% chance of being used in melee or range. When used the next weapon will be skipped.

commands.name: siegeweapon
commands.description: Equips the monster with a siege weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon will be used in locations that allow sieges, like cities and castles. Siege weapons are used in the first ten rounds of combat before any normal attacks are made.

commands.name: assassinweapon
commands.description: Equips the monster with an assassination weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon will be used to make an assassination attempt on an enemy before normal combat (including siege weapons) begins. Assassination attempts can only be used by the attacker and cannot be used against summoned creatures the summoner fails to control.

commands.name: prebatweapon
commands.description: Equips the monster with a prebattle effect weapon of this name that has a base damage of <dmg>. This weapon will be used before any normal combat (including assassination) begins.

commands.name: spellweapon
commands.description: Equips the monster with a Cast Spell weapon in the magic path specified. This spell weapon only has a 25% chance of being successfully used in melee combat.

commands.name: spellweaponbonus
commands.description: Equips the monster with a bonus Cast Spellweapon in the magic path specified. This spell weapon can be used in melee without penalty.

commands.name: spellweapon50
commands.description: Equips the monster with a limited Cast Spell Weapon in the magic path specified. This spell weapon has only a 50% chance of being used on any given combat round.

commands.name: spellweapon50s
commands.description: Equips the monster with a limited Cast Spell+skip weapon in the magic path specified. This spell weapon has only a 50% chance of being used on any given combat round. If it is used the next weapon will be skipped.

commands.name: spellweaponsingle
commands.description: Equips the monster with a limited Cast Spell Weapon in the magic path specified. Only one of the single spell weapons will be used per combat round if the monster has several

commands.name: more1spells
commands.description: The monster starts with more or fewer level 1 spells when it spawns.

commands.name: more2spells

commands.description: causes fear: 1=fear, 2=dread, 3=terror

commands.name: makeruin
commands.description: value = chance of turning current square into a ruin if possible

commands.name: meleeambush
commands.description: Will start in melee combat when ambushing

commands.name: poisoncloud
commands.description: spreads poison cloud, value = radius + 1

commands.name: poisonspikes
commands.description: AN poison strikeback

commands.name: acidblood
commands.description: AN acid strikeback, 50=50% of incoming damage

commands.name: forestheart
commands.description: takes control of nearby forests

commands.name: spread
commands.description: unit will position itself spread out among the other troops

commands.name: seduceaura
commands.description: attacker within this range might get seduced instead

commands.name: neverturn
commands.description: never draw facing the other way

commands.name: aigoldrally
commands.description: Hint that AI should go to recruitment loc when having lots of gold

commands.name: thrallhunt
commands.description: can create thralls (vampire)

commands.name: ainofollower
commands.description: AI hint to always use this commander as a leader (not a subcommander)

commands.name: putridexpl
commands.description: Putrid cloud upon death (value magic dmg + disease(MR))

commands.name: aimaxshop
commands.description: ai won’t buy more than this amount at the same place

commands.name: maxsum
commands.description: the maximum amount that can be summoned in a single battle

commands.name: changetemp
commands.description: makes square value degrees hotter

commands.name: likestoburn
commands.description: value% chance of wanting to burn a forest (wandering indep commanders only)

commands.name: reanimate
commands.description: reanimates automatically if possible, value = max amount / month

commands.name: diseasecloud
commands.description: spreads disease cloud, value = radius + 1

commands.name: mindexpl
commands.description: 1 = explodes in Mental Agony on Death

commands.name: deployoutside
commands.description: setup this unit outside fort in battles. The monster probably needs to be small (1x1 square) and few in numbers for the deployment to work properly, there is not much space left outside the walls before coming too close to the enemies.

commands.name: treelook
commands.description: sprite will be rotated and scaled randomly, like a random tree

commands.name: trample
commands.description: Can trample smaller unit for this amount of damage.

commands.name: tramplexsize
commands.description: Extra size regarding trampling. A size one trampling unit needs tramplexsize 1 to be able to trample anyone at all.

commands.name: autoastrology
commands.description: Superior Astrologist.

commands.name: desolator
commands.description: Drain value lifeforce from current square each month (like scourge lord pillar).

commands.name: desolcloud
commands.description: Spreads desolation cloud (exhaustion).

commands.name: diseaseshield
commands.description: Disease strikeback (MR negates).

commands.name: darkbless
commands.description: Has the dark blessing of a scourge lord

commands.name: defiler
commands.description: Needs to drain lifeforce to cast spells, range=max drain range.

commands.name: scourgedefiler
commands.description: Needs to drain lifeforce to cast spells of the defilement path, range=max drain range.

commands.name: petriaura
commands.description: Causes petrification like gorgon

commands.name: combustionaura
commands.description: Puts nearby units on fire

commands.name: confusionaura
commands.description: Confuses nearby units (easy MR negates)

commands.name: tunnelmove
commands.description: Tunnel teleporting in combat like a Purple Worm.

commands.name: siegetunnel
commands.description: Chance of emerging inside fort when storming.

commands.name: drawsize
commands.description: Draw the unit this amount of percent larger when shown on his unit token. Can be negative for smaller as well. Use this command to easily fine tune the units size to fit nicely in it token. Don’t use any large values as the resizing is not done everywhere in the game.

commands.name: evasion
commands.description: 25% chance to evade attacks.

commands.name: chopforest
commands.description: 1=can chop down forests.

commands.name: awakentrees
commands.description: Will awaken nearby trees & bushes in combat.

commands.name: awakenfungus
commands.description: Will awaken nearby mushrooms in combat.

commands.name: sitepopboost
commands.description: Will boost indep generation at current site (100 = +100%).

commands.name: slimeshield
commands.description: Slime strikeback

commands.name: transport
commands.description: Is a ship and can transport value amount of size 1 units.

commands.name: airbreather
commands.description: This wateronly unit will not drown on land

commands.name: vassal
commands.description: Is a vassal knight and will get part of yearly consription.

commands.name: sleeper
commands.description: Chance of starting a battle asleep if defending.

commands.name: snowsleeper
commands.description: Chance of starting a battle asleep if defending and it is snowy.

commands.name: deepsleeper
commands.description: Must receive at least 1-value dmg in one hit to wake up.

commands.name: selectclass
commands.description: Selects the class to be modified. The selected class is referred to as the active class. Class numbers are listed in Table Class numbers .

commands.name: newclass
commands.description: Creates a new class. The new class is automatically assigned a class number from the range of free numbers.

commands.name: setclassname
commands.description: Sets name for the class (e.g. "Dwarf Queen" or "Necromancer" or “Baron”) This command must be the first command after creating a new class.

commands.name: classdescr
commands.description: Sets the description for the class. The text must be on one line. The ^ symbol may be used for paragraph breaks.

commands.name: classabdescr
commands.description: Sets the description for the ability section of the class. The text must be on one line. The ^ symbol may be used for paragraph breaks.

commands.name: hometerr
commands.description: Sets the home terrain (home citadel) for the class. This terrain must be a citadel or the player will lose immediately when the game begins. This command is mandatory for a new class.

commands.name: clearstartterr
commands.description: Clears the starting terrain list for the class. This means any additional farms, hamlets, mines etc that the class would start the game with.

commands.name: addstartterr
commands.description: Adds extra terrain types that the class starts with when the game begins, such as extra farms, hamlets or mines.

commands.name: likesnorth
commands.description: A value from -10 to 10 indicating the willingness to have a northern start location.

commands.name: likessouth
commands.description: A value from -10 to 10 indicating the willingness to have a southern start location.

commands.name: likescoast
commands.description: A value from -10 to 10 indicating the willingness to start near the coast.

commands.name: startplane
commands.description: Starting citadel should be on this plane. If you use this command you should also use the "createcit" command and the terrain set as hometerr should be set to a gateway/pit/spire terrain. The hometerr terrain will be created in Elysium as a portal to the other plane.

commands.name: createcit
commands.description: This is the citadel terrain for classes with a different start plane.

commands.name: clearstartunits
commands.description: Clears the starting army for the active class.

commands.name: setmaincom
commands.description: Sets the main commander for the class. For example, the main commander for the Baron class is Baron and the main commander for the Barbarian class is Barbarian Leader. If the main commander does not appear in the recruitment list for the class, he cannot be replaced if lost.

commands.name: addstartcom
commands.description: Adds a starting commander to the class. All starting units added after the commander will appear already assigned to that commander’s squad at the beginning of the game. The main commander should not be added as a startcom.

commands.name: addstartunits
commands.description: Adds <nbr> monsters to the starting army for the class. Use this command multiple times to assign several different types of monsters (for example spearmen and archers).

commands.name: clearrec
commands.description: Clears the recruitment list for the active class.

commands.name: addunitrec
commands.description: Adds a monster to the recruitment list for the active class. The chance is a percentage chance that this unit can be recruited each month. The gold die is an open ended die that will be added to the base gold cost of the unit.

commands.name: addmercrec
commands.description: This command works like addunitrec, but the recruitment is mercenary and listed in green color. Mercenaries can only be recruited once and do not count against recruitment limits.

commands.name: addcomrec
commands.description: Adds a commander to recruitment list.

commands.name: recxcost
commands.description: The previous entry in recruitment list will get an additional cost of a special resource (not gold or iron). See table Resource Types for resource types.

commands.name: templerec
commands.description: The previous entry in the recruitment list will have increased chance of occurring, depending on the number of temples owned.

commands.name: libraryrec
commands.description: The previous entry in the recruitment list will have increased chance of occurring, depending on the number of libraries owned.

commands.name: reclimiter
commands.description: This will alter the requirements for the last added recruitment. string can be something like "+Baron" to require a Baron, "-Baron" to require the Baron to not be alive or "=Dwarf Worker" to require dwarf workers to be upgraded into the new troops.

commands.name: stdtroops
commands.description:
Adds standard troops to recruitment list. Standard troops are spearmen, swordsmen,
archers, crossbowmen, heavy infantries and catapult. Standard troops also include the chance of recruitment offers from Captain (20%) and Scout (10%).

commands.name: nostdtroops
commands.description: Standard troops are not available to the class.

commands.name: recwizchance
commands.description: This command sets an extra chance for recruitment offers from human wizards. The default value is 0.

commands.name: recherochance
commands.description: This command sets an absolute value for the chance for recruitment offers from human heroes. The default value is 1.

commands.name: recasschance
commands.description: This command sets an absolute value for the chance for recruitment offers from human assassins. The default value is 2.

commands.name: townbonusdescr
commands.description: This text will be shown as a description of the bonus for owning towns.

commands.name: libbonusdescr
commands.description: This text will be shown as a description of the bonus for owning libraries.

commands.name: templebonusdescr
commands.description: This text will be shown as a description of the bonus for owning temples.

commands.name: humancost
commands.description: cost multiplier (100=normal) for human recruitment at special locations (castles, desert palaces), 999=impossible

commands.name: mercpricemult
commands.description: value 2 = mercs will be twice as expensive

commands.name: mercboost
commands.description: value 100 = mercs will be twice as frequent, -50 = half as frequent

commands.name: recterr
commands.description: The previous entry in the recruitment list can only be recruited in this terrain.

commands.name: goldbonus
commands.description: Percentage bonus to gold income. For example, a bonus of 25 means that the class will have a 25% bonus on all gold income like the Baron.

commands.name: ironbonus
commands.description: Percentage bonus to iron income. For example, a bonus of 25 means that the class will have a 25% bonus on all iron income like the Baron.

commands.name: tradebonus
commands.description: Percentage bonus to trade income. For example, a bonus of 50 means that the class will have a 50% bonus on all trade income like the Senator.

commands.name: aiclass
commands.description: -1=AI players will never get this class by random choice, 0=normal, 1=this class can only be played by AI players

commands.name: classforestcit
commands.description: Can use ancient forests as citadels, like the Troll King.

commands.name: classwoodencit
commands.description: Can use watch towers as citadels, like the Senator.

commands.name: classminecit
commands.description: Can use mountain mines as citadels, like the Dwarf Queen.

commands.name: classcitterr
commands.description: Can also use this terrain as citadels. There can only be one classcitterr per class, but it can be combined with the 3 previous commands.

commands.name: reqterr
commands.description: The class requires at least one square of this terrain to be present on a map to play. This must be a terrain type that is normally present on maps. There can only be one reqterr per class.

commands.name: classtune
commands.description: Sets the class specific tune to this sound number. Tune sound numbers are 125-150 (class specific tunes) and 155-168 (general tunes).

commands.name: otherplanar
commands.description: Will enable the class to survive without owning a citadel in Elysium. Note that all classes will survive when owning their start citadel, even if it is not in Elysium.

commands.name: selectterr
commands.description: Select the terrain to be modified. Select a low number to alter an existing terrain or select a number between 500 - 999 to create a new terrain. Press ctrl-i in game on a terrain to see what number it has.

commands.name: spr
commands.description: Sets the image file for the terrain square.

commands.name: name
commands.description: Name of the terrain type.

commands.name: gold
commands.description: Gold income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: iron
commands.description: Iron income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: trade
commands.description: Trade value of the terrain when owned.

commands.name: herbs
commands.description: Herb income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: fungus
commands.description: Fungus income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: weed
commands.description: Weed income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: sacr
commands.description: Sacrifice income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: dead
commands.description: The location starts with <nbr> * d6 corpses in it.

commands.name: hands
commands.description: Hands of Glory income for the terrain when owned.

commands.name: gems
commands.description: A bitmask value that determines the gem income of the location. See the Gem Income Bitmask table. Note that you can add multiple 1 income values together to create a higher income value of a certain type of gem. Maximum income for a single gem type is 7.

commands.name: pop
commands.description: A value indicating the size of humanlike population. Farm = 5, City = 50.

commands.name: lifeforce
commands.description: Sets amount of lifeforce that can be drained from the square * 10. A plain has 10 and a forest 30. Negative values means square drain lifeforce with this radius (Pillar of Power has a value of -1).

commands.name: apcost
commands.description: Action Point cost for moving through the terrain.

commands.name: clearspec
commands.description: Clears the special attributes of the selected terrain.

commands.name: clearfort
commands.description: Clears the fort attributes of the selected terrain.

commands.name: citadel
commands.description: The terrain functions as a citadel when owned.

commands.name: batmap
commands.description: Associates the terrain with a certain battle map. See table Battle Maps . This is usually used for fortified locations, but villages also have a battle map.

commands.name: walls
commands.description: The location has walls in battle and is a siegable location.

commands.name: woodengate
commands.description: The fort has a wooden gate

commands.name: irongate
commands.description: The fort has an iron gate

commands.name: enchantedgate
commands.description: The fort has an enchanted gate

commands.name: bramblegate
commands.description: Bramble gate

commands.name: barricade
commands.description: Wooden barricade gate

commands.name: earthbarricade
commands.description: Earth barricade gate

commands.name: cloudgate
commands.description: Cloud gate

commands.name: magicwalls
commands.description: Ethereal units cannot pass through walls at this fort

commands.name: burnable
commands.description: The terrain can be burned like forest.

commands.name: water
commands.description: The terrain is water and cannot be passed, unless it is frozen or the monsters moving through it are amphibian or aquatic.

commands.name: cave
commands.description: The terrain counts as a cave.

commands.name: nostdrec
commands.description: Standard class based recruitment lists are not available in this terrain. Instead, there are other units available for recruitment specific to the terrain.

commands.name: ownable
commands.description: The terrain can be claimed for ownership if it provides income the player can use.

commands.name: smoke
commands.description: Pixels with a certain pink color (245,0,255) will produce smoke. Pixels with color (235,0,255) will produce flames and smoke.

commands.name: goldboost
commands.description: The terrain provides a global boost to gold income when owned.

commands.name: ironboost
commands.description: The terrain provides a global boost to iron income when owned.

commands.name: tradeboost
commands.description: The terrain provides a global boost to trade points when owned.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description: Structures with this command get double gold income during bumper harvest events. Farms have this attribute.

commands.name: invisible
commands.description: The sprite will not be drawn, instead the look of the terrain will be procedurally generated. Not a useful command for modding.

commands.name: visible
commands.description: Makes sure that the sprite is drawn as terrain and nothing else. Necessary to modify the look of procedurally drawn terrains like forests, mountains and villages.

commands.name: forest
commands.description: The terrain counts as forest for the purposes of abilities like Forest Stealth.

commands.name: swamp
commands.description: The terrain counts as swamp for the purposes of abilities like Swamp Move.

commands.name: mountain
commands.description: The terrain counts as a mountain for the purposes of abilities like Mountain Move.

commands.name: desert
commands.description: The terrain counts as a desert for the purposes of abilities like Desert Move.

commands.name: deepspawn
commands.description: Hybrid fishermen can appear here.

commands.name: melts
commands.description: A hint to the AI that the terrain melts after the winter. Frozen lakes and rivers have this attribute. Not a useful command for modding.

commands.name: nostart
commands.description: Players cannot start in this type of terrain. Other squares can be overwritten by a start citadel from a player.

commands.name: woodencitadel
commands.description: Can be used as citadel by the Senator

commands.name: forestcitadel
commands.description: Can be used as citadel by the Troll King.

commands.name: useable
commands.description: There is a special power inherent to the terrain that can be activated by commander actions.

commands.name: rare
commands.description: The terrain is a rare special terrain. It is sometimes deployed at a random place in Elysium by the random map generator.

commands.name: unique
commands.description: This terrain is unique and can only be placed once by the random map generator.

commands.name: mine
commands.description: The terrain counts as a mine.

commands.name: farsight
commands.description: The terrain gives increased vision range when there are units present there. Watchtowers and some citadels have this attribute.

commands.name: nosight
commands.description: The terrain does not provide vision into adjacent squares when owned. Forests and swamps have this attribute.

commands.name: temple
commands.description: The terrain counts as a temple.

commands.name: el
commands.description: Terrain starts as converted to the worship of El.

commands.name: settlement
commands.description: Defines the terrain as a human settlement. Hamlets, villages, towns etc have this attribute.

commands.name: void
commands.description: The terrain is part of the void. It is possible to both walk, swim and sail here.

commands.name: voidret
commands.description: The terrain is connected to the Void. Use for Pyramids and other such structures.

commands.name: library1
commands.description: Library level +1.

commands.name: library2
commands.description: Library level +2.

commands.name: hoburg
commands.description: All starting corpses here will be small size.

commands.name: snowok
commands.description: Income in this terrain is not affected by snow.

commands.name: desertok
commands.description: Terrain will survive surroundings being turned into desert.

commands.name: invseason
commands.description: Seasons are reversed in this terrain.

commands.name: spreadcold
commands.description: The terrain square spreads cold around it, turning nearby squares snowy.

commands.name: tempimmune
commands.description: The terrain will not be transformed into a wasteland when it gets too hot

commands.name: ritrebate
commands.description: All rituals cast on this location will be cheaper.

commands.name: bonusrelics
commands.description: Get this number of extra relics from this location. By default the amount of relics is one less than the amount of sacrifices earned.

commands.name: nosnowpen
commands.description: No movement penalty from snow.

commands.name: farvis
commands.description: Can be seen from far away.

commands.name: seepast
commands.description: Far horizon (like sea).

commands.name: port
commands.description: Ships can enter this terrain.

commands.name: realport
commands.description: Ships can be recruited here.

commands.name: misty
commands.description: Mist emanates from here.

commands.name: mistrare
commands.description: Will reduce the amount of mist produced. Rare is the chance in percent that mist will be produced.

commands.name: anchored
commands.description: Dimensionally anchored location.

commands.name: hardfly
commands.description: Difficult to fly here, costs 2 AP.

commands.name: nevercold
commands.description: This square will never get cold.

commands.name: ug
commands.description: This is an underground terrain.

commands.name: town1
commands.description: One town point.

commands.name: town2
commands.description: Two town points.

commands.name: cityname
commands.description: This terrain should start with a random city name.

commands.name: nodrown
commands.description: No one will drown in this terrain. Fishes can be on land and vice versa here. Used for frozen water tiles.

commands.name: destroyto
commands.description: Turns into this terrain when destroyed or burned up. Usually this command is not needed and it the terrain will be turned into something appropriate depending on its attributes.

commands.name: selectterrgroup
commands.description: Select the terrain group to be modified. The number must be between -1000 and -1199. The numbers between -1 and -999 are reserved for standard CoE5 and cannot be modified.

commands.name: setname
commands.description: Sets the name for the terrain group, e.g. "forests and temples".

commands.name: addterr
commands.description: Adds a terrain to this group. Negative numbers cannot be used here. By default a terrain group is empty.

commands.name: remterr
commands.description: Removes this terrain from the group.

commands.name: addallforests
commands.description: Adds all different forest terrains to the group. Jungles are not included.

commands.name: addalljungles
commands.description: Adds all different jungle terrains to the group.

commands.name: addallsettlements
commands.description: Adds all different human settlement terrains to the group.

commands.name: invert
commands.description: Inverts the contents of the group. Very useful when making a group that should contains all terrains but one.

commands.name: newritpow
commands.description: Creates an entire new school of rituals called a ritpow. This should be the first command when creating a new batch of rituals.

commands.name: newritual
commands.description: Create a new ritual with this name. This should be the first command for each new ritual.

commands.name: selectritual
commands.description: The optional value offs can be used to select a ritual other than the first one with this name. 0=the first one, 1=the second ritual with this name.

commands.name: ritpow
commands.description: Sets the ritpow used. If command is not used, the latest created newritpow will be used. Existing ritpow numbers can be found in the Ritual schools (pow nbr) table.

commands.name: level
commands.description: The level of the ritual. Usually the level is between 1 (apprentice level) and 3 (master level).

commands.name: cost
commands.description: Adds a resource cost to the ritual. E.g. cost 4 10 to add a cost of 10 sacrifices. A single ritual can have at most 4 different costs.  See table Resource Types for resource types.

commands.name: terr
commands.description: Restrict ritual to this terrain only. Negative numbers can be used for special terrain combinations.

commands.name: copyritual
commands.description: Copies all stats and abilities (except pow nbr and name) from another ritual to the current one.

commands.name: clearritspec
commands.description: Removes all special attributes from a ritual. This is only useful when modifying existing rituals.

commands.name: addstring
commands.description: Adds some text data to a ritual. Most often used to set what is summoned by a summoning ritual, but it depends on what effects are in the ritual. All addstring commands will be processed before any other commands for the ritual, so it does not matter where in the ritual you place them.

commands.name: summoning
commands.description: The ritual will summon the monsters specified in a random "string". Use addstring to add up to 15 strings with monsters. The string should be written like these examples:"1d6*Goblin", "c*Captain & 2d6*spearman & 2d4+2*Archer", "Purple Worm". The c* indicates a commander and 2d6 means two 6-sided dice will determine the number of monsters summoned. Dice cannot be combined with commanders.

commands.name: farsummon
commands.description: Like summoning, but it will occur at target location instead of at the caster’s location.

commands.name: sum0chance
commands.description: Use with summonings. Percent = chance of first "string" to be used instead of a random string among the others.

commands.name: sum1chance
commands.description: Use with summonings. Percent = chance of second "string" to be used instead of a random string among the third and later.

commands.name: sum2chance
commands.description: Same but one higher.

commands.name: sum3chance
commands.description: Same but one higher.

commands.name: sum4chance
commands.description: Same but one higher.

commands.name: sum0snow
commands.description: Works like sum0chance, but it can only succeed if there is snow at the target location.

commands.name: defctrl
commands.description: Default control chance for summonings. Can be overridden by monster’s own ctrlchance.

commands.name: varcost
commands.description: Set variable sacrifice amount (50=50-150%, 100=0-150%)

commands.name: raisedead
commands.description: Raises humanoid corpses from the dead.

commands.name: raiseanimals
commands.description: Raises animal corpses from the dead.

commands.name: specpow
commands.description: Makes a druid summoning, 1=minor, 2=major

commands.name: setplayer
commands.description: Following summons will be owned by this player. Default owner is the current player. Player -1 resets the owner to the default.

commands.name: promotion
commands.description: Promote existing units to another monster type. Use addstring to add promotion pairs, the first string sets a source unit and the second one the destination units. Multiple of these pairs can be added to a single ritual.

commands.name: transformtarg
commands.description: Will transform target into the unit type set by addstring. Value 1 = standard (use this), 2 = transform into following unit if level is high enough.

commands.name: newrit
commands.description: Grants a new ritual of this level.

commands.name: gainrit
commands.description: Learns the ritual that is offset numbers away. E.g. offset 1 = learn the following ritual when casting this one.

commands.name: rebatelvl
commands.description: This ritual will be half price if caster is this level or higher.

commands.name: levelup
commands.description: Will level up if caster is below this level. Leveling up means becoming a new monster determined by the mastery monster command.

commands.name: levelupmon
commands.description: Like levelup, but the new monster type is set by the addstring command. Set the new monster type in the addstring command.

commands.name: newspell1
commands.description: Learns one new level 1 combat spell from this path.

commands.name: newspell2
commands.description: Learns one new level 2 combat spell from this path.

commands.name: newspell3
commands.description: Learns one new level 3 combat spell from this path.

commands.name: forgetrits
commands.description: Forgets all known rituals.

commands.name: levelreq
commands.description: Caster must be exactly this level to use this ritual and cannot have another power at higher level.

commands.name: resrestrict
commands.description: Caster cannot have this resistance bitmask. Useful values are 2^4 for undead, 2^20 for immortal and 2^26 for ethereal.

commands.name: resreq
commands.description: Caster must have this resistance bitmask.

commands.name: benrestrict
commands.description: Caster cannot have this beneficial bitmask

commands.name: fxreq
commands.description: Unit must have 1+ in this fx to learn and cast this ritual. This command is probably not useful for modding.

commands.name: nomonworldreq
commands.description: Monsters in addstring "(-)…​" in the world must be fewer than limit. Default limit is 1.

commands.name: nomonplayerreq
commands.description: Monsters in addstring "(-)…​" in the world and owned by the current player must be fewer than limit. Default limit is 1.

commands.name: nomonmasteryreq
commands.description: Monsters in addstring "(-)…​" must not be in the world and owned by the current player unless level is higher than ritual requires

commands.name: nomonelysiumreq
commands.description: Monsters in addstring "(-)…​" must not be in elysium/sky/agartha. Monster in addstring "(+)…​" will disable following minuses if monster fulfills same requirement. This applies for all nomon… commands.

commands.name: nomonreq
commands.description: Monsters in addstring "(-)…​" must not be at current location.

commands.name: nomonhomereq
commands.description: Monsters in addstring "(-)…​" must not have their home at current location.

commands.name: fewmonreq
commands.description: The monsters in addstring "(-)…​" must not be more than max at current location.

commands.name: minmonreq
commands.description: The monsters in addstring "(&)…​" must be at least 'min' in number at current location.

commands.name: monworldreq
commands.description: At least min number (default 1) of the monsters in addstring "(&)…​" must be in the world. The min attribute is optional and can be omitted.

commands.name: monplayerreq
commands.description: At least min number (default 1) of the monsters in addstring "(&)…​" must be in the world and owned by the current player. The min attribute is optional and can be omitted.

commands.name: enchherereq
commands.description: This type of Enchantment must be active where there ritual is cast.

commands.name: free

commands.name: start
commands.description: will start with this ritual(s), no others

commands.name: nostart
commands.description: never start with this ritual (or learn from mastery)

commands.name: rarestart
commands.description: reduced chance of starting with this ritual

commands.name: notforpoor
commands.description: units with more expensive rituals can’t get this one

commands.description: demons never know this ritual

commands.name: nofemale
commands.description: females never know this ritual

commands.name: apcost

commands.description: Units with this fx nbr get 50% rebate

commands.name: rebateterr50
commands.description: Ritual cost is 20% cheaper in this terrain

commands.name: terrboost

commands.name: terrscale50
commands.description: +50% number of summoned monster when done in this terrain
