commands.name: chooseterrloc
commands.description: Player will choose target location for ritual.

commands.name: randterrloc
commands.description: Sets loc to a random terrain of this type on active plane.

commands.name: randomloc
commands.description: 1=random land loc, 2=many dead (excluding present), 3=rand enemy com, 4=rand enemy citadel, 5=home citadel

commands.name: randnewloc
commands.description: Like previous, but try to find an unknown location first.

commands.name: newlocplanes
commands.description: Like randnewloc but will go to other planes if necessary (but not hades)

commands.name: chooseloc
commands.description: Player choose target location. 2=deviate to many dead, 3=empty mirror req, 4=empty gold mirror, 5=horror mark deviation

commands.name: planeloc
commands.description: Shift target loc to same position but on another plane (neg = toggle between this plane and elysium).

commands.name: setplane
commands.description: Following randomloc etc. commands will be restricted to this plane

commands.name: choosefxtarg
commands.description: Player will choose a target unit that has this fx nbr.

commands.name: mirrortarg
commands.description: Set targ to an empty mirror unit, attr = size for mirror, -1=any size

commands.name: montarg
commands.description: Sets targ unit to a random unit at target location among the type added by addstring.

commands.name: scryloc
commands.description: Scry in a circle around target location.

commands.name: scatterscry
commands.description: Scry in a scattered way around target location.

commands.name: squarespec
commands.description: Adds special square flags to square. The only useful values are 2^14 (16384) converted to El, 2^16 (65536) poison fog, 2^17 (131072) strange mist.

commands.name: reducetown
commands.description: Reduces settlement at target location one step in size.

commands.name: destroyterr
commands.description: Destroys any valuable terrain at target location.

commands.name: alterloc
commands.description: Changes target square to this terrain.

commands.name: makeportal
commands.description: Connect this square to other portals of the same number. Portal nbr 1000 is special and will create a unique number.

commands.name: centerloc
commands.description: Center map on target location.

commands.name: trollifyloc
commands.description: Transform forest at target location into a troll forest.

commands.name: squareench
commands.description: Puts an enchantment at target location.

commands.name: planeswap
commands.description: Swaps target square with corresponding square on this plane.

commands.name: portalroom
commands.description: Creates a portal to a location around this terrain.

commands.name: movehome
commands.description: Moves home citadel location to target square.

commands.name: putcorpses
commands.description: Creates a number of human corpses in the target square (as if a fight involving humans had taken place there). Add 10000 to nbr in order to make the number of corpses scale with the sacrifice amount used.

commands.name: teleportloc
commands.description: Teleport target unit to target location. Attribute value 2 means the caster’s entire army is teleported to the target location.

commands.name: selectfx
commands.description: Sets mod-fx-nbr to this value. Used by next command.

commands.name: setfx
commands.description: Gives target unit a fx of type mod-fx-nbr and sets it to this value.

commands.name: fillmirror
commands.description: Puts a number of images into a mirror, -1 = fill to default value (mirrorammo)

commands.name: killtarg
commands.description: Gives between 1 and <dmg> amount of damage to target unit.  Use a value of  9999 for autokill.

commands.name: updatehome
commands.description: Updates home for target unit to where he stands. This is used to make some immortals resurrect in the correct place.

commands.name: bentarg
commands.description: Gives a beneficial bitmask to the target unit. See table Special Benefits . Particularly useful values for rituals are 2^26 to get the twiceborn effect or 2^24 to get the Stygian Bath effect. Note that most ben effects are temporary any will disappear after battle or during the turn and will be useless for rituals.

commands.name: afftarg
commands.description: Gives an affliction bitmask to the target unit. See table Special Afflictions . (New for version 5.16)

commands.name: bentargall
commands.description: Like bentarg, but also affects all the target’s followers.

commands.name: setvar
commands.description: Set the generic modding variable to this value.

commands.name: bentargvar
commands.description: Like bentarg, but the unit will only be affected if he is located in the terrain in the generic modding variable.

commands.name: cureoneaff
commands.description: Has this chance of curing one affliction on the target unit.

commands.name: insanity
commands.description: Gives insanity to the target unit. Negative value can be used to cure insanity. Only works if target is a commander.

commands.name: soundfx
commands.description: Play this sound effect.

commands.name: transformtarg
commands.description: Target unit will be transformed into one of the monsters added by addstring. Normally you want to use mode 1. Mode 2 will transform the units into higher monsters if they have higher skill level than necessary to cast the ritual.

commands.name: gainbless
commands.description: Percent chance of gaining a bless effect.

commands.name: gaindarkbless
commands.description: Percent chance of gaining a dark bless effect.

commands.name: ornext
commands.description: This ritual will have one of two possible effects. The first effect will consist of the following command, the next effect will consist of the remaining commands. Percent is the chance of the first effect happening.

commands.name: ornext2
commands.description: This ritual will have one of two possible effects. The first effect will consist of the two following commands, the next effect will consist of the remaining commands. Percent is the chance of the first effect happening.

commands.name: ornext3
commands.description: This ritual will have one of two possible effects. The first effect will consist of the three following commands, the next effect will consist of the remaining commands. Percent is the chance of the first effect happening.

commands.name: ornext4
commands.description: Like the other ornext commands.

commands.name: ornext5
commands.description: Like the other ornext commands.

commands.name: castertarg
commands.description: Sets target unit to caster.

commands.name: closewin
commands.description: Closes the ritual window after the ritual has completed.

commands.name: failplayer
commands.description: Failed summons will be owned by this player.

commands.name: centercaster
commands.description: Center map on caster.

commands.name: unfollowtarg
commands.description: Removes all followers from the target, should he be a commander that is commanding any units.

commands.name: simulacrum
commands.description: Creates a simulacrum.

commands.name: enchreqterr
commands.description: Enchantment will be auto dispelled if it is outside this terrain.

commands.name: forgetcurrit
commands.description: Caster will forget this ritual after casting it.

commands.name: seteventvar
commands.description: set this event variable to 1

commands.name: cleareventvar
commands.description: set this event variable to 0

commands.name: addeventvar
commands.description: increases the value of this event variable by 1

commands.name: subeventvar
commands.description: decreases the value of this event variable by 1

commands.name: aiwhere
commands.description: restricts the AI to only cast ritual in this terrain

commands.name: aialways
commands.description: AI will always (if chance = 100 try to cast this ritual, but not make any long time plans for it. chance=999 is special and means the AI will also make plans for the ritual.)

commands.name: airare
commands.description: Reduces the chance of the AI trying to use this ritual. Chance is the chance of casting the ritual and can be from 1-99. -1 is a special value meaning never cast it.

commands.name: aiweakonly
commands.description: AI commander will only cast this ritual if his troop strength is below this value. One spearman gives 10 troop strength points.

commands.name: aionlyplane
commands.description: AI will only cast ritual when on this plane

commands.name: aitarg
commands.description: For long range rituals. 1=try to target squares with enemy commanders, 2=try to target valuable squares with corpses in

commands.name: ainothere
commands.description: AI will not cast ritual in this terrain

commands.name: ainotclose1
commands.description: AI will not cast ritual if close to this terrain, radius=1

commands.name: ainotclose2
commands.description: AI will not cast ritual if close to this terrain, radius=2

commands.name: ainotclose3
commands.description: AI will not cast ritual if close to this terrain, radius=3

commands.name: ainotnearhome
commands.description: AI should not cast this ritual close to home (mindist = nbr of squares away)

commands.name: aiapprspam
commands.description: AI will dedicate apprentices to stay at home and only spam this ritual. Chance is 0-100

commands.name: ainosimul
commands.description: No more than one commander may plan to cast this ritual at once

commands.name: airestrig
commands.description: AI will always try to cast this ritual if it has at least this many of the primary resource for the ritual

commands.name: aimaxcast
commands.description: An AI player will never cast this ritual more than this number of times in a game

commands.name: sample
commands.description: Sets a sample file (sample.sw) as a certain sound effect number (sound). The sound effect number can be between 0 and 249, high numbers (170+) will create new samples and low number will replace the old samples that already occupies those numbers. The sample file should have the .sw (mono) or .sw2 (stereo) extension and be saved as a signed 16-bit 22050 Hz sample.

commands.name: sampleismusic
commands.description: Turns this sample into one a class specific tunes. That means it will loop into a background tune when it has finished playing. If you create a sample as a class specific tune, this must be used on that sample to keep the music playing. If used on a background tune it will remove that tune from the loop of background music.

commands.name: sampleisloopmusic
commands.description: Turns this sample into one of the background tunes. That means it will loop into another background tune when it has finished playing.

commands.name: playercolor
commands.description: Sets the default color for a player. Each color value is between 0 and 255.

commands.name: playerevent
commands.description: Once for each player every turn, occurs in home citadel by default

commands.name: squareevent
commands.description: For each player and each square in the world every turn

commands.name: endevent
commands.description: All events must end with this command

commands.name: +squareowner <player>
commands.description: True if target square is owned or occupied by this player.

commands.name: +armyowner <player>
commands.description: True if square is occupied by this player.

commands.name: +turnnbr <turn nbr>
commands.description: True if the current turn number is this turn nbr. Games start at turn 0 and any turn 0 events are executed before each player can player their first turn. But events are also run once before the game has started for anyone at turn -1.

commands.name: +minturnnbr <turn nbr>
commands.description: True if the current turn number is this turn nbr of greater.

commands.name: +chance <percent>
commands.description: Trigger has percent chance of being true.

commands.name: +player <player>
commands.description: True if current player has this player number.

commands.name: +class <player> "class name"
commands.description: True if this player is this class.

commands.name: +humanplayer <player>
commands.description: True if this player is a human player (not an AI player).

commands.name: +aiplayer <player>
commands.description: True if this player is an AI player. Only real AI players are valid, not the different independent factions.

commands.name: +hascom <player> "commander’s name"
commands.description: Also sets target unit.

commands.name: +hascomhere <player> "commander’s name"
commands.description: Also sets target unit.

commands.name: +ownsloc <player> <terr nbr>
commands.description: True if player owns this terrain anywhere in the world.

commands.name: +ownsloctarg <player> <terr nbr>
commands.description: True if player owns this terrain anywhere in the world. Also sets target location to this place.

commands.name: +terrain <terr nbr>
commands.description: True if target square is of this terrain.

commands.name: +season <0-3>
commands.description: 0=summer, 1=autumn, 2=winter, 3=spring.

commands.name: +seasondelay <1-3>
commands.description: 3=early (guaranteed to only happen once per season, 2=mid, 1=late).

commands.name: +varequal <var> <value>
commands.description: var = 0-9999, true if variable equals value.

commands.name: +varlesser <var> <value>
commands.description: True if the variable is less than value.

commands.name: +vargreater <var> <value>
commands.description: True if the variable is greater than value.

commands.name: +hasunit <player> "monster name"
commands.description: True if player has this kind of unit somewhere in the world. Also sets target unit (player -1 = any player)

commands.name: +hasunithere <player> "monster name"
commands.description: True if player has this kind of unit at current square. Also sets target unit (player -1 = any player)

commands.name: +hasitem <player> "item name"
commands.description: True if player has this kind of magic item somewhere in the world. Also sets target unit to wielder (player -1 = any player)

commands.name: +hasitemhere <player> "item name"
commands.description: True if player has this kind of magic item in current square. Also sets target unit to wielder (player -1 = any player)

commands.name: +squarename “square name”
commands.description: True if square has this name. e.g. “Crab Harbor” or “The Old Tower”

commands.name: +plane <planenr>
commands.description: True if target square is on this plane. See table Plane Numbers . The special values -1 (all planes) and -2 (Elysium-near planes) can also be used.

commands.name: +mincorpses <nbr>
commands.description: True if at least this many corpses of any type are present in the square.

commands.name: +minhumancorpses <nbr>
commands.description: True if at least this many human corpses are present in the square.

commands.name: +minhumanoidcorpses <nbr>
commands.description: True if at least this many humanoid corpses (humans, hoburghers, giants) are present in the square.

commands.name: +minanimalcorpses <nbr>
commands.description: True if at least this many animal corpses (of any type) are present in the square.

commands.name: +hasaffunithere <player> <aff>
commands.description: True if player has a unit in the current square that has all the afflictions in the aff mask. See table Special Afflictions . Also sets target unit (player -1 = any player)-

commands.name: +squareactivated
commands.description: True if active square is in its activated state. Terrains like Stone Henges can be (de)activated and their status can be checked with this trigger.

commands.name: +varvarequal <var1> <var2>
commands.description: var = 0-9999, true if variable 1 equals variable 2.

commands.name: +varvarlesser <var1> <var2>
commands.description: var = 0-9999, true if variable 1 is lesser than variable 2.

commands.name: +varvargreater <var1> <var2>
commands.description: var = 0-9999, true if variable 1 is greater than variable 2.

commands.name: addresources
commands.description: Adds an amount of resources to a player. See table Resource Types for resource types.

commands.name: message
commands.description: Sends a text message to a player.

commands.name: newunits
commands.description: also sets target unit

commands.name: promoteunits
commands.description: also sets target unit

commands.name: alterterrain
commands.description: changes the terrain of the current location

commands.name: killsquare
commands.description: kills everyone in target square

commands.name: namesquare
commands.description: Sets name of square, e.g. “Crab Harbor” or “!2The Old Forest” or “!!The Old Tower”

commands.name: removecorpses
commands.description: Removes this many corpses from target location. Nbr must be a positive value.

commands.name: removehumanoidcorpses
commands.description: Removes this many humanoid corpses from target location. Nbr must be a positive value.

commands.name: removeanimalcorpses
commands.description: Removes this many animal corpses from target location. Nbr must be a positive value.

commands.name: holdit
commands.description: 1=Any independent units on this square will hold and not move away. This holdit flag is cleared if the square is conquered or if any unit is spawned on it.

commands.name: setloc
commands.description: Move target location to a fixed location. Cannot be used on squareevents.
section_path: Change where the target location is

commands.name: randloc
commands.description: Move target location to a random location. See table Plane Numbers . The plane special values -1 (all planes) and -2 (Elysium-near planes) can also be used. Negative terrain numbers can also be used for special group of terrains. Cannot be used on squareevents.
section_path: Change where the target location is

commands.name: scatterloc
commands.description: Makes target location deviate a bit, can result in the same square. Cannot be used on squareevents.
section_path: Change where the target location is

commands.name: targunitloc
commands.description: Set target location to the place where the target unit is.
section_path: Change where the target location is

commands.name: comname
commands.description: Gives a new name to the target unit. Only works if the target is a commander.

commands.name: newitem
commands.description: Gives a specific magic item to the target unit.

commands.name: randitem
commands.description: Gives a random magic item to the target unit. Rare chance is the chance of being eligible for a rare magic item. It will always be an item that the target unit has appropriate equipment slots for.

commands.name: randmisc
commands.description: Gives a random magic misc item to the target unit. Rare chance is the chance of being eligible for a rare magic item.

commands.name: killunit
commands.description: Hits the target unit with this amount of damage. Use 9999+ for a purge that will disregard any special abilities the target might have (including immortality).

commands.name: gainxp
commands.description: Gives XP to the target unit. XP can be negative to remove XP.

commands.name: promote
commands.description: commanderize 0 = do not alter commander status, 1 = turns a non commander into a commander

commands.name: makestationary
commands.description: Makes target unit stationary on world map.

commands.name: makeblind
commands.description: Makes target unit blind.

commands.name: makediseased
commands.description: Makes target unit diseased.

commands.name: makenhwound
commands.description: Gives target unit a never healing wound.

commands.name: cureoneaff
commands.description: Cures one affliction.

commands.name: changeowner
commands.description: changes ownership of unit to this player

commands.name: makeaff
commands.description: Gives an affliction to target unit. See table Special Afflictions .

commands.name: makeben
commands.description: Gives a special benefit to target unit. See table Special Benefits . (New for version 5.16)

commands.name: makeminoraff
commands.description: Gives a random minor affliction to target unit.

commands.name: setvar
commands.description: var = 0-9999, sets a variable to a value

commands.name: addvar
commands.description: var = 0-9999, adds a value to a variable

commands.name: copyvar
commands.description: var = 0-9999, copies variable 1 to variable 2

description.text: description "Populum (latin for People) mod's goal is to link all the classes together in a thematic story-like fashion based loosely on systems of government connecting to social, political, and economic attributes. Populum increases the depth of the economy management and expands the early and late game of the classes by introducing new options.^^Some classes are meant for the AI only and are tagged with an '(NPC)' at the end of the class name. I would not recommend using these NPC classes because they are designed to be played by the AI with significant bonuses. These classes include: Goblin Emperor, Slave King, Independent Town, Bandit King, and the boss class called 'Blood Tide' which you may only have one due to the unique boss that comes with it. These classes were designed with the intent to be difficult early game enemies and mere nuisance to late-game players. The NPC classes are useful to quickly add flavor to a generated map. The NPC classes have their recommended difficulty built into the class name and are designed for the largest map size (enormous or custom larger). You may want to decrease an NPCs difficulty by one for 1-2 map size class reductions. For example the Goblin Emperor on enormous+ is played on Emperor difficulty; reduce to King for a Huge map, Duke for Large, Marquis for Medium, and anything smaller set to Count.^^Content Warning: This mod contains content (textual and game mechanics, not imagery) that may make some people uncomfortable including: Violence, Kidnapping and abduction, Enslavement, Death or dying, Pregnancy/Childbirth, Mental illness, Sexual Assault, Abuse, Animal cruelty or animal death, Self-harm and suicide, Eating disorders, Racism, Sexism and misogyny, and Classism."

descr "It is disputed whether the Minotaur is a beast or a humanoid, because it has been seen associating with both Brigands and Deer.  That it can wield and use weapons effectively speaks for humanoid, but the fact that the Minotaur cannot speak indicates it is a beast.  Until more research has been done, it is safest to assume that the Minotaurs are beasts and stay away or kill them when possible."

descr "The Purple Worms are truly gigantic in size and they eat the only thing that is available in the quantities needed to sustain such a huge thing, earth.  The worms are seldom seen despite their size, because they spend all their time deep below the surface of Elysium.  However those visiting the deep earth cannot miss the work of the worms as they walk in the vast empty caves left in the wake of the enormous worms.  Modern research proves that it was the Purple Worms that ate the parts that later became Inferno.  The devils settling there forced the worms to move closer to Elysium, where they currently reside and are likely to do so until something very powerful wants their newly created caverns for itself."
